newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed, account buying light.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed, account buying light.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in light, dealer-driven trade on Thursday as concern about shrinking T-bill supply offset a lack of account buying, analysts said.

"We have a situation here where people are not really considering too much the fundamentals, its more the potential scarcity value of these bills come next week's tender," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 2.89 percent from 2.88 percent at Wednesday's close.

The federal government has been shrinking the size of weekly T-bill tenders in the past several months. Next week the Bank of Canada will auction C$4.5 billion of T-bills, even as C$5.7 billion of T-bills mature.
With money markets yields so low, there was little interest on the part of accounts to buy T-bills at those levels, dealers said.

"The market has taken a long run down in rates here and I would have to say that from the account's perspective that they're a little bit more reluctant to want to step out the curve," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.21 percent from 3.19 percent. The one-year T-bill traded unchanged to yield 3.66 percent.

The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.05 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range. Normal settlement pressures from Tuesday's weekly T-bill auction are putting upward pressure on the call loan rate, dealers said.
